It is an old bug of the macOS version to automatically save opened attachments on the Desktop https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=238789 https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1387292

Setting the preference "browser.helperApps.deleteTempFileOnExit" to "True" is a good workaround: all those attachments scattered on your desktop disappear when you quit Thunderbird.

Eleven years ago I described a more elegant solution in this discussion in the MozillaZine forum https://forums.mozillazine.org/viewtopic.php?f=39&t=2948591

The ESR version will have a three cycle (at least 12 weeks) overlap between the time of a new release (153.0esr) and the end-of-life of the previous release (140.xesr). After that you'll be automatically upgraded to the 153.xesr series, and you'd remain on the ESR update channel.

The recommendation on one page regarding 153 is to switch from Release to ESR,

You're still on the ESR update channel. So that "recommendation" sounds silly to me. You need to decide what you want, and not follow some random, and out of context "recommendations".
